type1_consolidated:
## Appraisals
Students found the course structure praiseworthy, appreciating its well-organized and engaging content, logical progression, and punctual delivery. The course was commended for its comprehensive framework, clear explanations, and effective teaching methods, particularly in coding sections using Python. The evaluations were seen as highly effective and engaging, serving as valuable tools for quick review and preparation. The lecture slides were highly praised for their quality, design, and ability to ignite curiosity and provide clear explanations. The teaching assistants and professor were widely appreciated for their punctuality, deep subject knowledge, clear explanations, and interactive teaching methods, creating a supportive and encouraging atmosphere. Overall, the course was found to be both challenging and rewarding, with a positive learning experience supported by engaging and effective teaching methods.

## Criticisms
Students encountered numerous challenges across various aspects of the course structure, evaluation, and material. The scripting aspect was particularly difficult, with calls for more Python examples and clearer presentations. The course material was perceived as outdated and unengaging, with poor readability and numerous mistakes. Evaluations were criticized for their rigidity, stringency, and unfairness, with excessive difficulty and a focus on rote memorization. Lectures and practical sessions were often too fast or too slow, lacking sufficient examples and practical application. The course was found to be overly difficult and stressful, with a heavy workload and rushed assessments. Additionally, the course lacked positive elements such as helpful content or effective teaching methods, with many reviews suggesting a uniformly negative experience. The assessment methods were rigid and unfair, with the module being overly focused on assignments and projects rather than providing a supportive learning environment.

## Suggestions
To improve the course, students have highlighted several areas. For course material, they recommend adding extra training questions, easing practicals, and providing full answers for labs, along with more applied workshops and mock tests. In evaluation, they advocate for fewer, more comprehensive assessments, balanced question types, extended test durations, and more lenient marking, especially in midterms. For lectures, students suggest concluding them promptly, sharing slides earlier, using practical examples, and reducing the speed of instruction. They also call for more problem discussions, detailed explanations, and better organization of classes. Regarding course structure, students propose reducing the class burden, providing more hands-on workshops, clearer assignment directions, and longer exam and homework deadlines. They also request more accessible assistants, regular doubt-clearing sessions, and additional practice questions before lab sessions. Finally, students express a desire for more detailed lecture materials, supplementary recordings, and extra support from tutors and teaching assistants, while also suggesting the removal of unfair passing limits and the introduction of advanced modules like NLP.

They found the scripting aspect particularly challenging and called for more Python examples and clearer presentations. Overall, the course lacked positive elements such as helpful content or effective teaching methods, with many reviews suggesting a uniformly negative experience.

For evaluation, they advocate for greater fairness and consistency in grading, implementing the n- or n-1 rule to reduce stress, and making tasks more manageable. In course material, they recommend adding detailed explanations to lecture slides, breaking down projects into smaller assignments, and conducting preparatory sessions for labs and assignments. For lecture delivery, students suggest adjusting the pace to better suit different learning needs, clarifying the optional nature of the Topic Outline, and thoroughly covering fundamental topics. Across general areas, students propose fewer but more comprehensive assessments, easier practicals, and more applied workshops. They also call for prompt class conclusions, early slide sharing, practical examples, and reduced instruction speeds. Students further request more problem discussions, detailed explanations, and better class organization. To lighten the course burden, they suggest providing more hands-on workshops, clearer assignment directions, and longer exam and homework deadlines. They also advocate for more accessible assistants, regular doubt-clearing sessions, and additional practice questions before lab sessions. Lastly, students recommend more detailed lecture materials, supplementary recordings, and extra support from tutors and teaching assistants, while calling for the removal of unfair passing limits and the introduction of advanced modules like NLP.
